transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Um, thank you for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. I guess I'm here because... well, a few people at work have been mentioning that I'm a little hard to follow lately? I mean, I'm an artist, so I've always been a bit creative with how I explain things, right? But I guess my artist statements and my client notes have been sort of... jumping around. Like, I'll be talking about the texture of a piece, and then suddenly I'm talking about the budget, and then maybe something about, you know, the deeper, hidden meanings of it all. And my coworkers and clients are saying they can't quite understand what I'm trying to explain in meetings. It's probably just me being a little too passionate, but I wanted to make sure I'm doing everything right, you know? Does that make sense?

When you think back to how you were communicating and explaining things a year ago, before people started mentioning this, were you able to stay focused and organized in the same way, or is this jumping around something new that's started happening more recently?

Um, well... if I really think about it, I guess it's not entirely new? It's maybe been going on for... gosh, about a year and two months now? That was right around the time I made a big career move. I switched from doing community curation into full-time independent installation work. 

It's just such a huge shift, you know? Going out on your own. So I think I've just been really eager to share all my ideas at once, and maybe I just get a little ahead of myself. Is it normal to get a bit, um, scattered when you're taking on that much new responsibility? I really am trying my best to be professional and organized about it all, I promise. I hope that's an okay answer?
Over this past year or so, have you noticed any periods where you felt unusually energetic, needed less sleep than normal, or felt like your mood was higher or more elevated than your baseline?

Um, well... I guess there are definitely times where I feel really, really good? Like, for stretches of time, I just feel completely lit up. Almost unstoppable, honestly. It's like every single idea I have is just... brilliant. But I always just thought that was the good part of being an artist, you know? Catching that wave of inspiration and riding it. 

Though, I will admit... and I really hope this doesn't make me sound awful... sometimes when I'm in that zone, if a collaborator makes just a tiny comment or a small critique, I can get a little... well, I might snap at them. And I know it's a reaction that feels way bigger than the situation actually calls for. I always feel so terrible about it afterward, because I really do try to be a kind person to work with. Is that... does that happen to a lot of people when they're working hard? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.

When you feel that 'lit up' and unstoppable feeling, how long does that typically last? Are we talking about a few days, a week or two, or longer? And does it eventually come back down, or does it stay pretty consistent?

Um, well... I guess those really energized stretches, where I'm just bursting with projects and not really sleeping much, and maybe getting a little bit irritable like I mentioned... they don't just last a few days. If I'm being completely honest, and I hope this doesn't sound too strange, it feels like that's been kind of my normal for a while now? 

I'd say it's been going on for about ten months or so. It doesn't really come back down, it just sort of stays at that high level. I mean, I've been getting so much done, which is good, right? But I guess it has been a really long time to be running on that kind of fuel. Is it okay that it's lasted that long? I just assumed I was having a really productive year.

During these past 10 months when you've been feeling really energized and productive, has that feeling been pretty much constant the whole time, or have there been stretches where your mood came back down to normal before going back up again?

Um, well... it's not exactly that I'm just constantly at a hundred percent every single day for ten months straight. There are definitely times where things feel a bit calmer, and I guess my mood sort of settles back down to what feels more normal? 

But, um, if I'm really looking back at the whole year... I guess I'd have to admit that those really energized, kind of irritable, super-productive stretches have definitely taken up more of the year than the calmer parts. Even with it going up and down a bit, that high-energy feeling is definitely there the majority of the time. I really hope that doesn't make me sound too unstable or anything. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture... is it helpful to know that it fluctuates a little bit?

During those calmer periods you mentioned, when your mood settles back down to normal—would you describe that as just a return to your regular baseline, or have there been times where you've felt noticeably sad, down, or depressed below your normal level?

Um, no, not really. I mean, when the energy sort of tapers off, I just feel... normal again, I guess? Like I'm just back to being me, doing my regular routine. I don't really get, you know, super depressed or anything like that. I might feel a little tired just from working so hard, but it's not like I'm sad or down in the dumps. I'm generally a pretty positive person, I think. Does that make sense? I hope that's a good thing, that I don't really get depressed.
When you're in one of those really energized, productive stretches with lots of ideas and less need for sleep, how many days in a row does that typically last before things start to settle down?

Um, well, let's see... I guess when I'm really in the zone like that, it usually lasts for maybe... I don't know, a week? Sometimes maybe two weeks at a time? 

It's hard to say exactly because I'm just so focused on my art and getting things done. I don't really track the days too closely. But it's definitely a solid stretch of time before I kind of catch my breath and go back to my regular pace. Is a week or two a normal amount of time for that kind of creative burst? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of timeline... I hope I'm explaining it okay.

Looking back over this past year, have there been any stretches of time—maybe days or weeks—where you felt noticeably low, sad, hopeless, or where things felt kind of bleak or empty, even if it wasn't as intense as what you'd call clinical depression?

Um, no... really, honestly no. I think I'm pretty lucky that way. Even when things are quiet or I'm just resting after a big project, I don't get those dark or empty feelings. I just feel kind of... peaceful? Or just, you know, normal. 

I don't ever really feel hopeless or sad like that. I always try to look on the bright side of things, and I really love my work, so that keeps me pretty upbeat. I hope that's helpful... it's a good thing, right, that I don't get those low periods? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the answers you need.

When you're in one of those really energized, productive stretches—the ones that last a week or two—do you remember the shortest one of those? Like, what's the minimum number of days in a row you'd say you've felt that way before things settled down?

Um, let me think about that... I guess the shortest one? Maybe... maybe like four or five days? 

I'm not completely sure, to be honest. Sometimes if I just have a smaller project, the energy doesn't need to last as long, so I'll just be really focused and upbeat for a few days before I kind of wrap it up and go back to normal. It's never just, like, a single afternoon or anything. It's always at least a few days of feeling really good and getting a lot done. 

Does that sound like a normal amount of time for a creative burst? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of details... I just don't want it to sound like I'm all over the place or anything, because I really do feel like I manage it well.

Over this past year, have there been any stretches of time—maybe a few days or longer—where you felt the opposite of that energized feeling? Like, where you felt slower, more withdrawn, had trouble getting out of bed, or just couldn't enjoy things the way you normally do?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I guess sometimes I might feel a little tired if I've been working really hard on a piece, but it's just normal tiredness, you know? Not like... not being able to get out of bed or anything like that. 

I always make sure I'm up and doing things. I don't really get withdrawn or anything. I like being around people and I always enjoy my art. I wouldn't say I ever feel slow or... or down like that. It's really just needing a good night's sleep after a busy few days. 

That's pretty typical, right? Just needing a little rest after working hard? I try really hard to keep a good balance, so I hope it doesn't sound like I'm struggling with that. I feel like I handle my downtime pretty well.
